newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat Auto to hire 2,000 workers.
newsitem.headline: Fiat Auto to hire 2,000 workers.

text.p: Italian car maker Fiat Auto on Tuesday confirmed that it is to hire an extra 2,000 workers in its Italian car plants due to rising car orders reflecting a national car buying incentive scheme.
Fiat said in a statement that due to the increased demand for cars in Italy and the also the good progress of Fiat sales in the European car market, it was taking on the extra employees.
The Italian government's car buying incentive scheme -- from January 7 to September 30 -- offers incentives for vehicle owner who trade in cars older than 10 years old to buy new ones.

Fiat's Turin-based car plant Mirafiori which produces Puntos, Mareas and Pandas will take on 1,000 extra workers, while the group's Melfi car plant in the south of Italy and Termoli on the Adriatic coast will take on an extra 600 workers.
Melfi makes Puntos and the similar-sized Lancia Y cars, while Termoli produces engines and gearboxes largely for Fiat's smaller cars.
Fiat said that it had already started to take on an extra 400 employees at Melfi and its engine plant at Pratola Serra, just outside Naples in the south of Italy.
